composition.serve_who: Sheet 108-01-150-001 "Steering System GA" is a BUILDING/STRUCTURAL GA (perspective view, plan view, sections, details, BOM table) showing the twin-rudder mechanical steering system: rudder blades, rudder stocks/bearings, tiller arms, rod links, autopilot ram, and the wheel-steering cable/sheave circuit. All callouts (upper/lower bearing structure, tiller arms, rod links, autopilot ram, sheave boxes, tracks, toe-in/Ackermann tables) name components that belong to the vessel's steering system, mirrored port/stbd. Register nodes served: 150-rudder-blades (rudder blades, bearings, stocks, tiller arms, toe-in geometry — matches established facts), 150-steering-system (wheel/cable/sheave mechanical steering infrastructure), 150-autopilot-system (autopilot ram and its mounting). BHD L, Tri-beams, partitions LM1/LM2 are hull structure providing mounting points, not equipment themselves — carried as facts on the equipment they support.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Section C-C shows rudder blade profile/rotation, BOM items 2-7,18 (rudder bearings, housings, retainer, rudder itself) all attach to the rudder stock; established fact [150-rudder-blades] already carries toe-in/Ackermann/3-path redundancy from this same sheet — this composition adds physical positions/specs.

functions.label: Rudder blade & stock assembly (port/stbd mirrored)
functions.what_it_does: Provides the steering surface; stock passes through hull via upper (180mm) and lower (220mm) bearing housings into the hull shell, retained top and bottom, water-tight sealed at the shell penetration.
key_components: rudder blade, FRP, ~107.5kg dry / 215kg wet ea (item 18)
functions.dry_data: Rudder dry mass 107.5kg, wet (assembled) 215kg each; bottom bearing housing GRP 4.7kg, top bearing housing GRP 3.4kg.
functions.sheet_region: Perspective view (upper-left), Section C-C (bottom-left, view rotated 26°), Detail D (scale 1:5)

functions.label: Rudder stock support structure
functions.what_it_does: Upper and lower bearing structures (detailed on separate drawings 108-05-151-001/002) carry the rudder stock loads into the hull; stock passes through partitions LM1 (port) / LM2 (stbd) and is supported at hull shell datum with G10 spacers (30mm) either side of the top bearing.
key_components: Partition LM1 (port), Partition LM2 (stbd, mirrors LM1)
G10 spacers 30mm x2 at top bearing
functions.dry_data: Stock support height 1685mm on outer skin / 1493mm datum-referenced (Section C-C); position ~1551mm & 2130mm on hull outer/inner skin per plan view dimensions.
functions.sheet_region: Perspective view; Section B-B (looking to port, partition LM hidden, scale 1:20); Detail D

functions.label: Toe-in / Ackermann steering geometry
functions.what_it_does: Sets rudder toe-in angle at neutral and differential inside/outside rudder angle vs car (wheel input) position, tuned via rod link length.
key_components: Rod link — carbon tube + bhd fittings + M16 ball joints (item 15)
functions.dry_data: Neutral toe-in 1.8° at rod link length 2044mm (established); table shows 0°@2025mm to 3°@2056mm. Ackermann: car position 0mm→inside 1.8°/outside -1.8°; 98mm→10°/6.3°; 212mm→20°/16.0°; 316.5mm→30°/25.3°; 364.3mm→35°/30.0°. Car race ±365mm from CL.

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Plan view and details A/E and Port Lower Sheave Box detail show the wheel-driven cable/sheave/tiller-arm mechanism distinct from the autopilot ram — this is the manual (2-wheel) steering path referenced in the established redundancy note ('3 independent systems: 2 wheels + pilot').

functions.label: Wheel-to-rudder cable/sheave steering circuit
functions.what_it_does: Transmits helm wheel input via Vectran line over aluminium sheaves through upper and lower sheave boxes, along a track-mounted car, to tiller arms on each rudder stock, driving both rudders in coordinated (Ackermann) fashion.
key_components: Track support with 16mm tapping plate insert (see dwg 108-01-150-006)
functions.dry_data: Sheave dry mass 1.4kg ea (10 off, 14.0kg total); tiller arm assembly (racing double filler arm) 40kg ea, 2 off; sheave boxes bonded per instruction to lie horizontal.
functions.sheet_region: Detail A (scale 1:10, top-center-left); Port Lower Sheave Box Detail (top-center-right, NTS); Plan view (scale 1:20); Detail E (scale 1:5, track support)

flow_scenarios.path: Helm wheel → Vectran line (20mm) over 100mm sheaves through upper sheave box (bonded to hull, at STN 10 area) → down through lower sheave box → track-mounted car (assembled car, item 13) travels ±365mm from CL on 1100mm track → car connects to both tiller arms via rod links → tiller arms rotate rudder stocks port and stbd in Ackermann relationship

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Plan view centre shows autopilot ram (item 19) with dedicated support callout ('AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT IS BOLTED THROUGH BHD L, bond tapping plates on fwd face') and a tri-beam penetration made specifically for pilot rod movement — a distinct actuator path from the wheel/cable circuit, matching the established '3 independent systems: 2 wheels + pilot' note.

functions.label: Autopilot ram actuation of rudder linkage
functions.what_it_does: Drives the steering car/linkage directly via a hydraulic/electric ram (300mm stroke) mounted through bulkhead BHD L, independent of the wheel cable circuit, giving the autopilot its own control path to both rudders per the 3-path redundancy scheme.
key_components: BHD L mounting with bonded tapping plates on fwd face
Tri-beam penetration sized for pilot rod movement
functions.dry_data: Ram total mass 40.0kg; metal construction; mounted centrally in plan view between the two tiller-arm/car assemblies.
functions.sheet_region: Plan view (scale 1:20), center; callouts 'AUTOPILOT RAM SUPPORT...' and 'MAKE PENETRATION IN TRI-BEAM TO SUIT PILOT ROD MOVEMENT'

flow_scenarios.path: Autopilot ram (bolted through BHD L, tapping plates on fwd face) extends/retracts through penetration made in tri-beam → drives the same car/rod-link mechanism as the wheel circuit → moves both tiller arms/rudders together; independent of wheel cable path so failure of either wheel steering does not disable autopilot control (established redundancy fact)

infrastructure.system_name: Hull structural support (Tri-beams, Bulkhead BHD L, Partitions LM1/LM2)
facts: Tri-beam 11 and Tri-beams 6+7 are structural members the steering assembly passes through/near; a penetration was made in a tri-beam specifically to suit pilot rod movement.
BHD L (bulkhead) carries the autopilot ram mounting, bolted through with bonded tapping plates on its fwd face.
Partition LM1 (port) and LM2 (stbd, mirrored) are bulkhead partitions the port/stbd rudder stocks pass near.
These are hull/structural items, not equipment — no equipment node fits; flagged as shared structural infrastructure.
